Name: GLOBAL:SOFAConventions
Comment: This conventions stores directivities of acoustic receivers (aka microphones) in the time domain in free field.

Name: GLOBAL:DataType
Comment: We store frequency-dependent data here

Name: GLOBAL:RoomType
Comment: The room information can be arbitrary, but the spatial setup assumes free field.

Name: GLOBAL:License
Default: No license provided, ask the author for permission

Name: GLOBAL:DatabaseName
Comment: Name of the database. Used for classification of the data

Name: GLOBAL:Description
Comment: Narrative description of a measurement including the device under test. For microphones, the measurement method or the standard used, e.g. substitution measurement with a 1/4 inch measurement. microphone and  point source speaker, conducted in anechoic chamber

Name: GLOBAL:ReceiverManufacturer
Comment: Manufacturer of the device under test

Name: GLOBAL:ReceiverModel
Comment: Model of the device under test

Name: GLOBAL:ReceiverSerialNumber
Comment: Serial number of the device under test

Name: GLOBAL:ReceiverFilterSetting
Comment: Entry whether a filter setting was used on the DUT, e.g. selectable directional characteristic, low-shelf, etc.

Name: GLOBAL:ReceiverTransducerType
Comment: The electro-acoustic transducer type e.g., small/large diaphragm condenser, electro-dynamic, etc.

Name: GLOBAL:ReceiverAcousticalOperatingPrinciple
Comment: The Acoustical Operating Principle, e.g. Pressure gradient transducer, Pressure transducer

Name: GLOBAL:ReceiverSymmetry
Comment: In which plane is the microphe considered symmetrical, e.g. None, horizontal, vertical, quarter, axial

Name: GLOBAL:ReceiverPolarPattern
Comment: The polar pattern of the microphone (e.g., hyper-cardiod). If individual patterns need to be stored for every receiver, it shall be provided by a custom string 'PolarPatterns' with dimensions RS, ES.

Name: ReceiverNormalization
Comment: 0: No or unknown normalization; 1: Normalized re ListenerView or SourceView (on-axis normalization); 2: Average removed (diffuse-field response). Reference: 1: DIN EN 60268-4, S. Weinzierl et. al. Handbuch der Audiotechnik. 2: Ackermann et.al. Musical instruments as dynamic sound sources

Name: ReceiverSensitivityReal
Dimensions: III, IRI, IIN, IRN, MII,MRI, MIN, MRN
Comment: Real part of the sensititvity of the microphone. If one sensitivity is provided it holds for all receivers.

Name: ReceiverSensitivityImag
Dimensions: III, IRI, IIN, IRN, MII,MRI, MIN, MRN
Comment: Imaginary part of the sensititvity of the microphone. If one sensitivity is provided it holds for all receivers.

Name: ReceiverSensitivityReal:Symbol
Comment: If sensitivity is provided, this shall be provided. It shall be mv/Pa, dBV or dBFs/Pa (for digital microphones)

Name: ReceiverSensitivityReal:MeasurementDescription
Comment: Describes the measurement method, e.g., at 500Hz, at 1kHz

Name: ReceiverMaxSPL
Comment: The maximum possible sound pressure level (SPL), can be given as a single value, single value for each receiver, one spectrum or a spectrum for each receiver

Name: ReceiverMaxSPL:Symbol
Comment: If MaxSPL is provided this shall be provided as well. It shall be dBSPL (dB re 20 µPa)

Name: ReceiverMaxSPL:MeasurementDescription
Comment: Describes the measurement method, e.g., equivalent electrical signal, tube measurement

Name: ReceiverEquivalentNoiseLevel
Comment: Self-noise is the signal the microphone produces of itself, even when no sound source is present. Can be given as a single value, single value for each receiver, one spectrum or a spectrum for each receiver

Name: ReceiverEquivalentNoiseLevel:Symbol
Comment: If EquivalentNoiseLevel is provided this shall be provided as well. It shall be dBSPL, A-weighted

Name: ReceiverEquivalentNoiseLevel:Description
Comment: Describes the measurement method, e.g., CCIR, A-weighted

Name: ReceiverMinOperatingFrequency
Comment: Minimum Frequency above which the measurement data is valid. E.g. band limitation of the microphone, etc.

Name: ReceiverMinOperatingFrequency:Units
Comment: If ReceiverMinOperatingFrequency is provided this shall be provided as well. It shall be hertz

Name: ReceiverMaxOperatingFrequency
Comment: Minimum Frequency above which the measurement data is valid. E.g. the frequency range of the excitation, band limitation of the microphone, etc.

Name: ReceiverMaxOperatingFrequency:Units
Comment: If ReceiverMaxOperatingFrequency is provided this shall be provided as well. It shall be hertz

Name: EmitterMinOperatingFrequency
Comment: Minimum Frequency above which energy is emitted by the source, so the measurement data is valid. E.g. the frequency range of the excitation, band limitation

Name: EmitterMinOperatingFrequency:Units
Comment: If EmitterMinOperatingFrequency is provided this shall be provided as well. It shall be hertz

Name: EmitterMaxOperatingFrequency
Comment: Minimum Frequency above which the measurement data is valid. E.g. the frequency range of the excitation, band limitation of the microphone, etc.

Name: EmitterMaxOperatingFrequency:Units
Comment: If EmitterMaxOperatingFrequency is provided this shall be provided as well. It shall be hertz

Name: ListenerPosition
Comment: Position of the microphone array during the measurements.

Name: ListenerPosition:Type
Comment: Type of the coordinate system used.

Name: ListenerPosition:Units
Comment: Units of the coordinates.

Name: ListenerView
Comment: Orientation of the microphone array

Name: ListenerView:Type
Comment: Type of the coordinate system used.

Name: ListenerView:Units
Comment: Units of the coordinates.

Name: ListenerUp
Comment: Up vector of the microphone array

Name: ReceiverPosition
Comment: Positions of the individual capsules during the measurements (relative to the Listener)

Name: ReceiverPosition:Type
Comment: Type of the coordinate system used.

Name: ReceiverPosition:Units
Comment: Units of the coordinates.

Name: SourcePosition
Comment: Position of the acoustic source (e.g. a loudspeaker)

Name: SourcePosition:Type
Comment: Type of the coordinate system used.

Name: SourcePosition:Units
Comment: Units of the coordinates.

Name: SourcePosition:Reference
Comment: Narrative description of the spatial reference of the source position, e.g., 'On the front plate between the low- and mid/high-frequency unit' for a loudspeaker. Mandatory in order to provide a reference across different sources.

Name: SourceView
Comment: View vector for the orientation.

Name: SourceView:Type
Comment: Type of the coordinate system used.

Name: SourceView:Units
Comment: Units of the coordinates.

Name: SourceView:Reference
Comment: Narrative description of the spatial reference of the source view, e.g., 'Viewing direction of the bell' for a trumpet or 'Perpendicular to the front plate' for a loudspeaker. Mandatory in order to provide a reference across different sources.

Name: SourceUp
Comment: Up vector of the acoustic source (loudspeaker or silentspeaker)

Name: SourceUp:Reference
Comment: Narrative description of the spatial reference of the source up, e.g., 'Along the keys, keys up' for a trumpet or 'Perpendicular to the top plate' for a loudspeaker. Mandatory in order to provide a reference across different sources.

Name: EmitterPosition
Comment: Position. In a simple settings, a single emitter is considered that is collocated with the source.

Name: EmitterPosition:Type
Comment: Type of the coordinate system used.

Name: EmitterPosition:Units
Comment: Units of the coordinates.

Name: EmitterDescriptions
Comment: A more detailed description of the Emitters. For example, this may be the strings of a violin or the units of a loudspeaker.

Name: Data.Real
Comment: Real part of the complex spectrum. The default value 0 indicates that all data fields are initialized with zero values.

Name: Data.Imag
Comment: Imaginary part of the complex spectrum. The default value 0 indicates that all data fields are initialized with zero values.

Name: Data.NormalizationReal
Comment: Real part of transfer function or gain-factor used for the normalization.

Name: Data.NormalizationImag
Comment: Imaginary part of transfer function or gain-factor used for the normalization.

Name: N
Comment: Frequency values. Only positive frequencies are considered (below aliasing frequency).

Name: N:Units
Comment: Units used for N
